title: xiom pkg install
concept: The `xiom pkg install` command resolves and fetches all declared dependencies
why: Declaring dependencies in a manifest is only half the story — you need to actually download them. `xiom pkg install` reads `package.xi`, solves the dependency graph, downloads crates from the registry, and sets up the local environment. It handles transitive dependencies automatically, so you declare what you directly use and the toolchain figures out the rest.
theory: `xiom pkg install` performs a multi-phase operation: (1) Parse `package.xi` and extract dependency declarations. (2) Resolve versions against the registry index, applying semver constraints. (3) Build a complete dependency tree, detecting conflicts. (4) Download each crate into a local cache (`~/.xiom/pkgs/`). (5) Generate `xiom.lock` with exact versions. (6) Make crates available for `use` statements. The command must be re-run after modifying dependencies in the manifest.
syntax_ref:
xiom pkg install                # install all deps
xiom pkg install <crate>        # add and install a single crate
xiom pkg install --update       # update all to latest compatible
code_template:
# Given package.xi with:
# dependencies:
#   xiom_json: "^0.4"

# Run in terminal:
# $ xiom pkg install
# Downloading xiom_json v0.4.2...
# Resolving dependencies...
# Generated xiom.lock

# Now usable in code:
use xiom_json

fn main() {
    let data = xiom_json::parse("{\"key\": 42}")
}
solution:
# Step 1: Edit package.xi
# dependencies:
#   xiom_net: "^1.2"
#   xiom_json: "^0.5"

# Step 2: Run install
# $ xiom pkg install
#   Fetching xiom_net v1.2.1
#   Fetching xiom_json v0.5.0
#   Fetching xiom_io v0.3.0 (transitive)
#   Generated xiom.lock

# Step 3: Use in src/main.xi
use xiom_net::http
use xiom_json

fn main() {
    let response = http::get("https://api.example.com/data")
    let parsed = xiom_json::parse(response.body)
    io.println("{parsed}")
}
tips: Run `xiom pkg install` after every `package.xi` edit
Use `xiom pkg cache clean` to free disk space from old packages
The lockfile ensures reproducible builds — commit it for binaries
common_mistakes: Editing source code to use a crate before running install — results in 'crate not found' errors
Forgetting `--update` when intentionally upgrading a dependency
Assuming `xiom build` automatically runs `pkg install` (it doesn't)
